scenes.en: A complete, simple guide.
scenes.say: Do you, or someone at home, have diabetes? Then this video is for you. In the next few minutes, we explain in simple words how sugar affects the eyes, the warning signs, and how to protect your sight.

scenes.en: The retina at the back works like the film in a camera.
scenes.ta: கண்ணின் பின்புறம் உள்ள ரெடினா, கேமரா ஃபிலிம் போல
scenes.say: First, how the eye works. Light enters the front of the eye and is focused on the retina, a thin layer at the back. The retina works like the film in a camera. It sends the picture through the optic nerve to the brain.

scenes.en: The retina is fed by very fine, delicate blood vessels.
scenes.ta: ரெடினாவுக்கு ரத்தம் தரும் மிகச் சிறிய குழாய்கள்
scenes.say: The retina needs a steady supply of blood, through very tiny, delicate blood vessels. These small vessels are the part that high sugar affects the most.

scenes.en: Over years, the tiny vessels weaken. They can leak or get blocked.
scenes.say: When blood sugar stays high for many years, the walls of these tiny vessels become weak. They can leak fluid or blood, or get blocked. This is called diabetic retinopathy.

scenes.en: It is the most common cause of vision loss in people with diabetes (NEI).
scenes.ta: சர்க்கரை நோயாளிகளின் பார்வை இழப்புக்கு முக்கிய காரணம்
scenes.say: Did you know? According to the National Eye Institute, diabetic retinopathy is the most common cause of vision loss in people with diabetes. The good news: early checks and good control can protect your sight.

scenes.en: Early on, there is no pain and vision can seem normal.
scenes.say: Here is the tricky part. In the early stage, there is usually no pain, and your vision can seem completely normal. Damage can start long before you notice anything.

scenes.en: Blurry or changing vision, dark spots, poor night vision, faded colours.
scenes.say: Later, you may notice warning signs. Blurry vision. Vision that changes from day to day. Dark spots or strings drifting across your sight. Poor vision at night. Or colours that look faded.

scenes.en: Fluid can collect in the macula, the reading area of the retina.
scenes.say: Sometimes fluid collects in the macula, the small central area of the retina we use for reading and seeing faces. This swelling can make reading and recognising faces difficult.

scenes.en: Changing glasses power, earlier cataract, higher glaucoma risk.
scenes.ta: கண்ணாடி பவர் மாறலாம், கேட்டராக்ட் சீக்கிரம் வரலாம்
scenes.say: Diabetes can affect the eyes in other ways too. Your glasses power can change when sugar levels swing. Cataract can come earlier, and the risk of glaucoma is higher.

scenes.en: Sudden vision loss, a curtain or shadow, a shower of new spots or flashes.
scenes.ta: திடீர் பார்வை இழப்பு – உடனே கண் மருத்துவரை பாருங்கள்
scenes.say: See an eye specialist urgently if you have sudden loss of vision, a curtain or shadow over your sight, a shower of new dark spots, or flashes of light. Do not wait for it to settle.

scenes.en: At least once a year, even if you see well.
scenes.say: Now, the most important step: a dilated eye exam, at least once a year, even if your vision feels fine. Your doctor may advise checks more often, depending on your eyes.

scenes.en: Drops widen the pupil so the doctor can see the whole retina.
scenes.ta: சொட்டு மருந்து போட்டு ரெடினாவை முழுமையாக பார்ப்பார்கள்
scenes.say: In this exam, eye drops widen the pupil, so the eye specialist can see the whole retina. It is painless, but your vision may be blurry and bright for a few hours. So go with a family member, carry sunglasses, and take your latest sugar reports.

scenes.big: Protect your eyes: A, B, C
scenes.en: Keep sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol in your target range.
scenes.say: Next, how to protect your eyes. Remember A, B, C. A for your average sugar test. B for blood pressure. C for cholesterol. Keep all three in the target range your doctor sets.

scenes.en: More vegetables, greens and whole grains. Fewer sweets and fried foods.
scenes.say: Eat well. Fill half your plate with vegetables and greens, choose whole grains like millets, and cut down on sweets, sugary drinks and fried food.

scenes.en: A brisk 30-minute walk on most days helps control sugar.
scenes.say: Move every day. A brisk walk of about thirty minutes on most days helps control sugar and blood pressure. Walk together. It is more fun.

scenes.en: Smoking harms the eye's tiny vessels. Never stop treatment on your own.
scenes.say: Do not smoke, because it harms the same tiny blood vessels. Take your diabetes treatment exactly as your doctor advises, and never stop it on your own.

scenes.big: Myth: “I see clearly, so my eyes are fine”
scenes.en: Fact: early damage has no symptoms. Only an eye exam can find it.
scenes.say: Myth: I see clearly, so my eyes are fine. Fact: early damage has no symptoms. Only an eye exam can find it in time.

scenes.en: Check your power once your sugar is stable.
scenes.ta: சர்க்கரை சீரான பிறகு கண்ணாடி பவர் பாருங்கள்
scenes.say: A useful tip. If your sugar has been very high, or has just changed a lot, your power may shift for a while. Get your glasses power checked once your sugar is stable, for an accurate prescription.

scenes.ta: வீட்டிலேயே கண் பரிசோதனை – முழு குடும்பத்துக்கும் ரூ.100

scenes.en: Not a diagnosis. See an eye specialist for your own eyes.
scenes.ta: இது பொது தகவல் மட்டும் – கண் மருத்துவரை அணுகுங்கள்
scenes.say: This video is general information, not a diagnosis. For your own eyes, see an eye specialist. Share this video with someone who has diabetes, and subscribe for more eye-care tips.
